skcm.description: Aggregates of melanocytes in the epidermis or dermis forming nest-like clusters.
Melanocytes with enlarged, irregular, hyperchromatic nuclei suggestive of malignancy.
Upward single-cell or small-cluster migration of melanocytes into the epidermis.
Loss of epidermal surface over tumor often accompanied by fibrin and inflammation.
Brown-black intracytoplasmic pigment within tumor cells or macrophages.
Lymphocytes within or adjacent to tumor indicating host immune response.
Mitotic activity within tumor cells reflecting proliferative rate.
Coagulative or geographic areas of cell death within the tumor.
Dense fibrous stromal response often surrounding invasive melanoma cells.
Fibrosis, melanophages, and vascular proliferation indicating prior tumor loss.

ov.description: Finger-like fibrovascular cores lined by tumor epithelium (common in serous tumors).
Concentric laminated calcified structures often seen in papillary serous tumors.
Non-uniform architecture with both solid tumor sheets and gland-forming areas.
Marked nuclear enlargement and irregularity indicating high-grade tumor cells.
Presence and frequency of mitoses as a marker of proliferation.
Focal or extensive tumor cell death often seen in high-grade ovarian carcinomas.
Reactive fibroblastic tissue within or surrounding tumor nodules.
Immune cell clusters within tumor stroma or at tumor–stromal interface.
Morphologic patterns distinguishing serous papillae from endometrioid glands.
Tumor spread or adhesion to the ovarian surface epithelium.

lgg.description: Neoplastic glial cells diffusely infiltrating white matter and cortex.
Irregular, hyperchromatic nuclei of glial cells indicating neoplastic change.
Eosinophilic, plump astrocyte-like tumor cells with abundant cytoplasm.
Small cystic spaces within tumor composed of vacuolated tumor or extracellular fluid.
Eosinophilic, corkscrew-shaped proteinaceous inclusions in long-standing gliosis/tumor.
Tumor cells clustering around neurons in gray matter.
Basophilic granular or psammomatous deposits within tumor tissue.
Observed mitoses indicating proliferative activity in glial tumor.
Tufts of proliferating endothelial cells forming complex vessels.
Areas of tumor cell death often with surrounding pseudopalisading cells.

ucs.description: Distinct malignant epithelial and sarcomatoid (spindle) tumor components.
Severe nuclear pleomorphism and hyperchromasia in tumor cells.
Spindle-shaped malignant cells resembling sarcoma within the tumor.
Extensive coagulative necrosis common in high-grade uterine carcinosarcoma.
Frequent mitoses reflecting aggressive tumor proliferation.
Tumor cells present within vascular or lymphatic channels.
Non-gynecologic mesenchymal differentiation such as cartilage or bone.
Epithelial component showing typical endometrioid or serous morphology.
Mixed inflammatory cells within stroma or tumor areas.

pcpg.description: Rounded nests of chief cells separated by delicate vascular stroma.
Polygonal chief cells with peripheral sustentacular support cells.
Highly vascular connective tissue between tumor nests.
Variation in nuclear size and shape among tumor cells.
Finely granular eosinophilic cytoplasm typical of neuroendocrine-like cells.
Glassy, eosinophilic stromal change often surrounding nests.
Focal cell death seen in more aggressive lesions.
Tumor breach of capsule indicating invasive behavior.

thca.description: Finger-like epithelial projections with fibrovascular cores.
Optically clear nuclei with dispersed chromatin characteristic of papillary thyroid carcinoma.
Longitudinal nuclear indentations seen in tumor cell nuclei.
Concentric calcified concretions within tumor stroma.
Small to large follicles containing colloid-like material.
Eosinophilic or pale extracellular substance within follicle-like spaces.
Tumor penetration through fibrous capsule into surrounding tissue.
Lymphoid aggregates and germinal centers in adjacent thyroid parenchyma.
Cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm from mitochondrial accumulation.

acc.description: Tumor cells arranged in nests separated by fibrous septa.
Cells with pink, granular cytoplasm typical of many adenocarcinomas.
Irregular, enlarged nuclei with hyperchromasia in tumor cells.
Counting mitoses to assess tumor proliferative index.
Focal areas of tumor cell death indicating aggressive disease.
Tumor cells invading blood vessels within or near the tumor.
Collagenous bands partitioning tumor nests or lobules.
Areas where tumor cells have clear, glycogen-rich cytoplasm.
Tumor extension through and beyond a capsule if present.

sarc.description: Elongated tumor cells arranged in fascicles or storiform patterns.
Swirling (storiform) or parallel (fascicular) arrangements of spindle cells.
Marked variation in nuclear size and shape among tumor cells.
Coagulative necrosis frequently present in high-grade sarcomas.
Abundant mitotic figures including atypical forms in malignant sarcoma.
Prominent or abnormal blood vessel formation within tumor.
Loose mucoid extracellular matrix imparting a gelatinous appearance.
Variable inflammatory cells mingled with tumor elements.
Components like bone or cartilage differentiating within the sarcoma.

esca.description: Keratinizing squamous cells or nests indicating squamous carcinoma.
Concentric whorls of keratinizing cells typical of well-differentiated squamous carcinoma.
Desmosomal connections between squamous cells seen microscopically.
Areas of gland formation indicating adenocarcinomatous components.
Tumor cell death often seen in ulcerated or high-grade lesions.
Proliferation of basal-type epithelial cells in adjacent mucosa.
Immune cells in the stroma or at the invasive front.
Reactive fibrous tissue surrounding infiltrating tumor glands or nests.
Surface loss of epithelium with granulation tissue and fibrin.

stad.description: Well-formed tumor glands producing lumenal structures and mucin.
Cells with peripheral nuclei and large intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles.
Extracellular mucin accumulation often with floating tumor cells.
Single or small clusters of discohesive tumor cells lacking gland formation.
Prominent collections of lymphocytes often at the tumor–stroma interface.
Dense fibrotic stromal response surrounding invasive carcinoma.
Areas of cell death often within rapidly growing tumor regions.
Tumor emboli identified within vascular or lymphatic channels.
Tumor tracking along or within nerve sheaths.

lusc.description: Concentric keratinized structures seen in well-differentiated squamous tumors.
Visible desmosomal connections between squamous tumor cells.
Premature keratinization of individual tumor cells.
Small basaloid cells with high N:C ratio forming nests or cords.
Coagulative necrosis frequently present in high-grade squamous carcinomas.
Mixed inflammatory cells in stroma or around tumor islands.
Fibrotic stromal response associated with invasive growth.
Loss of intercellular connections producing separated tumor cells.
Tumor extension along nerves indicating aggressive behavior.

lihc.description: Tumor cells arranged in thickened cords or trabeculae resembling liver plates.
Expanded hepatocellular plates with multiple cell layers.
Sinusoidal endothelial cells closely apposed to tumor cell plates.
Intracellular or canalicular bile pigment within tumor cells.
Cytoplasmic clear vacuoles consistent with fatty change in tumor or surrounding liver.
Formation of acinar-like spaces mimicking glandular structures.
Expansion of sinusoidal spaces between tumor cell trabeculae.
Peritumoral or intratumoral fibrotic bands often in chronic liver disease.
Irregular, enlarged hepatocyte nuclei within malignant foci.

dlbc.description: Monomorphic population of large lymphoid cells replacing normal tissue.
Large nuclei with scant cytoplasm typical of aggressive lymphoma cells.
One or more large nucleoli visible within tumor cell nuclei.
Frequent mitoses reflecting rapid tumor cell proliferation.
Coagulative or geographic areas of tumor cell death common in high-grade lymphoma.
Macrophages containing apoptotic debris indicating high turnover.
Fragmented apoptotic cells scattered through the tumor.
Variable collagenous tissue within or between lymphoma cell sheets.

prad.description: Neoplastic glands resembling prostatic acini with variable differentiation.
Large confluent glands with punched-out lumina forming sieve-like structures.
Tumor tracking along nerves commonly seen in prostate carcinoma.
Absence of basal cells around glands, supporting invasive diagnosis.
Large nucleoli within epithelial nuclei characteristic of prostate cancer.
Expansion of pre-existing ducts by high-grade malignant cells with retained architecture.
Dense stromal tissue of prostate intermingling with tumor glands.
Extracellular mucin pools or mucin-producing tumor cells in rare variants.
Chronic inflammatory cells present in stroma adjacent to tumor.

kirp.description: Combination of tubular and papillary formations lined by neoplastic epithelium.
Papillary stalks with central fibrovascular tissue supporting epithelium.
Glassy eosinophilic collagenous stroma often seen in papillary tumors.
Regions where cells contain glycogen-rich clear cytoplasm.
Pink granular cytoplasm in tubular epithelial tumor cells.
Enlarged, irregular nuclei indicating neoplastic transformation.
Focal tumor cell death associated with aggressive features.
Observed mitoses denoting proliferation rate of tumor cells.

uvm.description: Mixed cell morphologies of melanocytic tumor including spindle and epithelioid forms.
Intracellular melanin giving brown-black color to tumor cells.
Variation in size and shape of nuclei suggesting malignancy.
Tumor cell death sometimes seen in aggressive uveal melanoma.
Immune cells within stroma reflecting host response.
Tumor penetration into blood vessels, common route for metastasis.
Number of mitoses used for prognostic assessment.
Collagenous reaction around tumor nests or cells.

thym.description: Tumor arranged in lobules separated by fibrous septa mimicking thymic lobules.
Areas resembling thymic cortex (lymphocyte-rich) and medulla (epithelial-rich).
Epithelial whorls resembling normal thymic Hassall bodies when present.
Small, lymphocyte-like cells often abundant in thymic tumors.
Clusters of thymic epithelial tumor cells within lymphoid background.
Collagen bands partitioning the tumor into lobules.
Focal cell death occasionally present in higher-grade thymic neoplasms.
Clear perivascular zones sometimes seen around vessels in thymic tissue.

luad.description: Well-formed tumor glands or acinar structures signifying adenocarcinoma.
Tumor cells proliferating along intact alveolar septa without stromal invasion.
Tumor epithelial fronds often with fibrovascular cores.
Small tight clusters of tumor cells lacking fibrovascular cores associated with poor prognosis.
Tumor cells producing intracellular or extracellular mucin.
Tumor cell death evident as pale acellular areas or geographic necrosis.
Reactive fibroblast-rich connective tissue around invasive tumor.
Irregular, hyperchromatic nuclei indicative of malignancy.
Immune cells present within or around tumor tissue.

ucec.description: Endometrial-type glands formed by neoplastic epithelial cells.
Rounded squamous cell aggregates (morules) within endometrioid lesions.
Variation in nuclear size and shape indicating atypia.
Observed mitoses used to grade proliferative activity.
Focal areas of tumor cell death, more common in high-grade tumors.
Morphologic distinction between endometrioid glands and papillary serous areas.
Fibrotic stromal response surrounding invasive tumor glands.
Tumor cells present in vessels signaling metastatic potential.

cesc.description: Mature squamous cells with abundant keratin within tumor nests.
Sheets of basaloid squamous cells lacking prominent keratinization.
Small cells with scant cytoplasm forming tight nests or cords.
Desmosomal connections between squamous tumor cells seen on H&E.
Coagulative necrosis common in high-grade cervical cancers.
Immune cells within stroma and at tumor margins.
Reactive fibrous tissue accompanying invasive squamous carcinoma.

read.description: Neoplastic gland structures producing lumina and mucin.
Extracellular mucin collections often containing tumor cells.
Cells with large mucin vacuole displacing the nucleus peripherally.
Areas of cell death within tumor indicating aggressive biology.
Numerous immune cells within tumor stroma or mucosa.
Single cells or small clusters at invasive front associated with worse prognosis.
Dense reactive fibrosis at the tumor invasion front.
Tumor emboli identified in lymphatic or vascular spaces.

tgct.description: Large clear cells with central nuclei and prominent nucleoli typical of seminoma.
Fibrous bands containing lymphocytes partitioning tumor nodules.
Multinucleated trophoblastic cells occasionally present and producing hCG.
Solid sheets and gland-like structures with pleomorphic cells.
Microcystic or reticular architecture with Schiller-Duval-like features.
Areas of hemorrhagic necrosis common in mixed germ cell tumors.
Basophilic calcified deposits often present within tumor or stroma.
Blood extravasation within tumor suggesting vascular fragility or rapid growth.

coad.description: Neoplastic colon glands forming lumenal structures and producing mucin.
Back-to-back glandular structures with punched-out lumina.
Tumor regions rich in intracellular or extracellular mucin.
Mucin-laden cells with eccentric nuclei seen in diffuse-type tumors.
Tumor cell necrosis often seen in high-grade colorectal carcinoma.
Dense fibrous response at invasive fronts of colorectal tumors.
Mixed immune cell presence within tumor stroma and mucosa.
Tumor cells within vascular or lymphatic channels indicating spread.

meso.description: Papillary or tubular formations lined by mesothelial-type cells.
Elongated tumor cells forming fascicles or sheets in sarcomatoid areas.
Polygonal epithelioid tumor cells forming cohesive nests or tubules.
Fibrotic reaction often accompanying invasive mesothelioma.
Irregular enlarged nuclei within malignant mesothelial cells.
Focal cell death often seen in aggressive or advanced tumors.
Chronic inflammatory cells mixed within tumor and stroma.

kich.description: Sheets or nests of tumor cells with compact arrangement.
Pink granular cytoplasm seen in many chromophobe-like or oncocytic cells.
Clear zone around nuclei giving a halo appearance in some renal tumors.
Collagenous bands separating nests of tumor cells.
Areas of cell death indicating higher-grade behavior.
Variation in nuclear size and contour among tumor cells.
Glassy, eosinophilic stromal change often present in papillary areas.

brca.description: Tumor forming ducts that mimic or distort normal breast lobular units.
Well-formed tubular structures indicating glandular differentiation.
Back-to-back glandular structures with perforated lumina.
Severely atypical nuclei with coarse chromatin and pleomorphism.
Central necrosis within ducts forming comedo patterns in high-grade DCIS or invasive tumors.
Peritumoral or intratumoral lymphocytes indicating immune engagement.
Reactive collagen deposition and scarring associated with invasive disease.
Basophilic granular or laminated calcifications often seen in DCIS or tumor stroma.
Cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli.

hnsc.description: Concentric keratinized whorls indicating squamous differentiation.
Desmosomal connections between squamous tumor cells visible on H&E.
Small hyperchromatic cells forming nests or trabeculae.
Tumor cell death zones often present in ulcerated or high-grade lesions.
Mixed inflammatory cells including neutrophils and lymphocytes.
Surface epithelial loss with associated exudate and granulation tissue.
Dense fibrous tissue accompanying invasive tumor front.
Tumor encircling or invading nerve fibers, a poor prognostic sign.

chol.description: Malignant glands often lined by atypical biliary-type epithelium.
Dense collagenous reaction common in cholangiocarcinoma.
Intracellular or extracellular mucin secreted by tumor cells.
Tumor infiltration into or around nerves in the biliary tract.
Areas of tumor cell death, sometimes with hemorrhage.
Chronic inflammatory cells in tumor stroma or interface with liver.
Scarring both within tumor and in surrounding hepatic parenchyma.

blca.description: Exophytic fibrovascular fronds lined by urothelial tumor epithelium.
Expansion and hyperplasia of urothelial layers due to tumor.
Variation in nuclear size/shape indicating dysplasia or malignancy.
Areas showing keratinization or squamous morphology within urothelial carcinoma.
Tumor cell death which may be extensive in high-grade lesions.
Cohesive islands of tumor cells infiltrating lamina propria or muscle.
Mixed immune cells in stroma or at the mucosal surface.
Tumor penetration into detrusor muscle indicating advanced stage.

kirc.description: Cells with optically clear cytoplasm due to glycogen/lipid content.
Tumor cells arranged in nests separated by delicate vasculature.
Prominent thin-walled capillaries crisscrossing tumor nests.
Encapsulating fibrous tissue around tumor margins in some cases.
Coagulative necrosis within tumor often indicating rapid growth.
Variation in nuclear size and shape across tumor cells.
Areas where tumor cells have abundant pink cytoplasm instead of clear cells.
Glassy homogeneous stromal change often accompanying tumor nests.
